A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed and demonstrated a radiation-hard 0.25μm silicon-on-sappphire (SOS) complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS) technology for the ATLAS pixel detector at the Large Hadronic Collider (LHC).
we have demonstrated that the technology is robust and can be used for radiation hard applications.
the radiation response of a standard 0.25μm silicon-on-sappphire CMOS process is excellent for use in radiation environments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the radiation hardness of a 0-25 μm silicon on sapphire CMOS technology can be improved by the use of enclosed layout transistors (ELTs).
the technology is well suited for radiation environments and that it can be used to build a large number of ASICs for the ATLAS pixel detector.
the radiation response is not dominated by the leakage current of the individual devices, but by the leakage current through the interconnects.
